problem: Existing 2D attacks on VLMs (pixel noise, patches) are misaligned with the 3D world and only work from fixed views. Existing 3D attacks target traditional vision models (point-cloud nets, detectors) and do not transfer to cross-modal VLMs. As a result, the robustness of VLM-driven VLN perception to adversarial physical objects has not been evaluated.
motivation: VLN agents increasingly use VLMs for scene perception and semantic mapping, so a misperceived object can propagate into localization and goal actions and make the task fail. In service-oriented deployments (delivery, assistive robots) this is a reliability and QoS risk, and it calls for an attack that is object-specific, consistent between 3D and 2D, and robust across views.
key_idea: Detect and cluster the victim object in 3D, then optimize a bounded 3D point-cloud perturbation using masked VLM image-text feature losses plus 3D color and Chamfer regularization, fusing per-view updates weighted by view importance.
insight: Localizing the victim object in 3D and restricting the VLM feature losses to the object mask (with a background-preserving term) keeps the attack object-specific, and importance-weighted iterative fusion across views makes it stable. The ablation (Table 'ablation') removes Alignment, L2d, L3d and Fusion one at a time and reports that each one matters. Without alignment the SAM 2D positions are disordered and miss the true 3D location. Fusion is credited with stable convergence. The exact ablation numbers are not visible in the provided text.
method: Victim Object Alignment: LLaVA checks which scenes contain the victim label, Grounding DINO plus SAM produce masks and scores, masks are back-projected to 3D, and DBSCAN clusters them into discrete objects. One cluster is chosen at random as the victim.

Adversarial Object Render: The adversarial object is O+δ, a point-cloud-wise 3D perturbation bounded by ||δ||_p≤ε (32/255). It is projected to 2D views with the camera intrinsics and extrinsics and depth.
Geometric Feature Regularization (L3D): An L2 color-similarity loss plus a Chamfer distance keep O_adv close to O in color and shape.

Masked VLM Feature Regularization (L2D): Cosine-similarity losses on mask-restricted VLM features: image-to-image (to the victim image for untargeted attacks, to a target image for targeted ones), image-to-text (toward the target label embedding), and a background-to-background term (weights α=0.5, β=0.01).
View importance weighting: Each view's weight is its Grounding score plus the fraction of pixels covered by the object, normalized across views.

Iterative Adversarial Object Fusion: Per-view local perturbation updates are fused into a global 3D perturbation. An update is rejected and its weight lowered if the MSE to the prior view's perturbation is ≥μ1 (0.01), and the perturbation bound is reduced if the L2D discrepancy is ≥μ2 (0.05). Up to Max attempts per view, 200 Adam iterations.

setting.backbone: Attack targets frozen VLN agents: VLMaps (LSeg), CoWs (CLIP), CF (CLIP-Fields), ORION (interactive). LLaVA, Grounding DINO and SAM are used in the attack pipeline.
setting.training_data: none (the attack is optimized per victim object; the victim agents are used zero-shot as released)
setting.observation: RGB-D egocentric images turned into point clouds and semantic maps
setting.action_space: primitive rotate / move / stop actions of the agents (continuous environment)
setting.privileged: White-box access to the agent's VLM in the main setting (black-box via proxy agents in the transfer experiments); attacker can modify scene objects and collect environment data

numbers_note: The main result tables (overall, label accuracy, transfer, ablation) are in external files not included in the text, so no numeric values are available. Only the confidence example (chair 0.44→table 0.81) and transfer decline figures (max 25.0% across encoders, 7.9% across datasets) appear in the text. This is an attack paper and not a standard navigation benchmark.
results: AdvOF outperforms the 2D attacks MF and AdvCLIP and the 3D attacks ST and TT3D on all four agents (VLMaps, CoWs, CF, ORION), degrading SR/SPL/KPA on attacked scenes while preserving normal-scene performance, according to the text. It changes the perception of one object precisely (chair 0.44→table 0.81) and stays effective across near and far views. It transfers across image encoders (max drop 25.0%) and scene datasets (max drop 7.9%). Black-box transfer to other VLMs is weaker but comparable to baselines in the white-box setting, and it is robust to shear, scaling, noise and brightness changes.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation (Habitat) with perturbed RGB-D data; no physical-world printing or 3D-printing test.
Black-box transfer across VLMs drops significantly compared with white-box.
Only perception is attacked, on zero-shot agents; the victim object is picked at random and the attack needs the agent's VLM in the white-box setting.
